title: Capability manifest
description:
GET /api/bridge/capabilities — what this runtime can actually do right now.

A hint, not a guarantee: a service can stop between discovery and invocation, so authoritative failure always arrives as a typed run error. An unavailable capability must still be LISTED with a reason — omitting it makes 'installed but stopped' indistinguishable from 'never heard of it', and the caller cannot tell the user whether to install something, start something, or give up.

protocol.description: Protocol the sender speaks. Receivers reject unknown majors rather than guessing.

runtime.description: Where execution happens. A capability is offered by a runtime, not by the platform in the abstract.

id.description: Dotted capability id. `oaiy.*` is reserved for the platform; products and plugins own their own namespace (`connector.aokie.*`).

reason.description: Why a capability is not usable right now. Closed set so a caller can branch on it; `detail` carries the sentence a person reads.

detail.description: Actionable sentence naming what to install or start. Never 'coming soon'.

connections.description: Connection ids that can satisfy this capability. Ids only — a connection's credentials never cross the bridge.

pluginId.description: Set when a plugin contributes this capability.
